function: Learned policy selects random-access pilots (or backoff) and uplink transmit powers; MMSE channel estimation and ZF/MR combining are classical, activity detection assumed perfect (p. 3, p. 4, p. 9).
notes: Exclude, function. p. 1: "We develop a distributed, cross-layer policy that allows the users to dynamically and independently choose their pilots and transmit powers". p. 9: the output module has "two sub-modules for generating the pilot selection probabilities and the transmit power". The learned decisions are random-access pilot selection with backoff (access control, above the PHY) and continuous uplink power control (a PHY decision), so check 4 passes by the joint rule. But the learned method does not detect symbols, estimate the channel, or design beams: p. 3: "we assume perfect pilot detection", the channel estimate is the classical MMSE estimate (p. 3, eq. 6), and the BS applies MR or ZF combining (p. 4). Its metrics are the maximum normalized packet drop rate and the sum effective throughput (p. 10), so none of the seven areas applies. If the reviewer regards uplink power control in random access as radio resource management above the PHY, the code would be above_phy instead; the exclusion holds either way. The BS has M = 100 antennas and the results are simulated (p. 10-13), so checks 6 and 7 would not apply. The PDF is arXiv 2410.17068v1 (22 Oct 2024) and prints no DOI or journal; Crossref gives this DOI the same title and authors in IEEE TCCN.
